chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, from Aban ibn Taghlib, and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran and Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How should I say to her when I am alone with her?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should say,

I marry you as a Mut'a marriage upon the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), neither inheriting nor being inherited from, for such and such days, and if you wish, such and such years, for such and such dirhams, and you specify the compensation which you two agree upon, whether little or much. So when she says 'Yes', she has consented, so she is your wife, and you are the closest of people to her.

I said, 'But I am shy to mention the stipulation of the days.' He said, 'It is more harmful to you.' I said, 'And how?' He said, 'If you do not stipulate, it becomes a permanent marriage, and maintenance becomes obligatory upon you during the waiting period, and she becomes an heir, and you cannot divorce her except by a Sunnah divorce.'

key_terms.لَا مَوْرُوثَةً: Nor being inherited from (referring to the husband not inheriting from the wife by default)
key_terms.لَا وَارِثَةً: Neither inheriting (referring to the wife not inheriting from the husband by default)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct formula for contracting a Mut'a marriage according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the precise verbal formula for Mut'a, emphasizing that explicit stipulation of duration and dowry is essential to distinguish it from permanent marriage (Nikah al-Mumaddad). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that omitting the time limit converts the union into a permanent marriage, thereby incurring lifelong maintenance and inheritance rights, which underscores the juristic importance of clear contractual terms in Shia fiqh.
